about:
Axial Industries Ltd. is a bearing supplier headquartered in Iowa City, Iowa. The company has been sourcing and supplying bearings and related products for more than 30 years, growing into a distributor for the agricultural and industrial manufacturing markets.

The company distributes a full line of bearings — including AG disk harrow bearings, taper roller bearings, mounted units, needle roller bearings, water pump bearings, stamped flanges, double row ball bearings, radial ball bearings, angular contact bearings, oil seals, sprockets and pulleys — sourced from premium and value brands worldwide. Axial also offers machining, extrusion and die‑casting capabilities, and operates flexible delivery, stocking and warehousing programs from its Iowa facility. A dedicated office in China supports global supplier qualification and product identification.

Axial serves customers across automotive and transportation, agriculture and construction, energy and utilities, industrial machinery and automation, defense and marine, mining and metals, medical and pharmaceutical, and food and beverage sectors. Its clientele ranges from OEMs to maintenance operations that require reliable bearing solutions to keep production lines running.

The company emphasizes responsive, knowledgeable service — every inquiry reaches a specialist with decades of bearing experience — and maintains rigid quality standards to ensure shipments match exact specifications. Its stated goal is to eliminate sourcing headaches by delivering the right product on time, at competitive prices.

name: Axium Packaging CA Plant
old_description: With unrivaled engineering expertise, in-house design and tool shops, and uniform equipment platforms across 22 manufacturing sites, Axium reduces development and shipping lead-times from weeks to days.
about:
Axium Packaging’s California plant operates in Ontario, a facility opened in 2013 as part of a company founded in 2010 by the Judge Family Group. The business began with a bottle manufacturing launch in Mississauga, Ontario, Canada, and is led by CEO Pushminder Judge and President Paul Judge. Ownership remains with the Judge family, and the company holds minority-certified status.

The plant produces rigid plastic packaging using extrusion blow molding, injection stretch blow molding, injection blow molding, injection molding, and tube extrusion, supplemented by decoration and finishing services. Across the network, Axium runs 33 facilities totaling more than 4.7 million square feet of manufacturing space with a workforce exceeding 3,500. The integrated platform includes in-house design studios, 3D modeling, and tool shops that support concept-to-shelf development.

Customers span personal care and beauty, healthcare and nutraceuticals, food, beverage and spirits, and home and fabric care. The company serves multinational brands such as Unilever, Procter & Gamble, L’Oréal, Bath & Body Works, and Diageo, often through near-site manufacturing arrangements that shorten supply chains.

Axium differentiates itself with a speed-to-market model that cuts traditional lead times in half, a vertically integrated recycling subsidiary (Vertix) that supplies post-consumer recycled resin, and a unified quality system built on GFSI FSSC 22000 V6 standards across all sites.

name: Axon Circuit, Inc.
old_description: Axon Circuit, Inc. is a printed circuit board manufacturer headquartered in Tampa, Florida.
about:
Axon Circuit, Inc. is a printed circuit board manufacturer headquartered in Tampa, Florida. The company was founded in 1990 and has operated continuously in the Southeast United States for over three decades.

The firm produces rigid PCBs ranging from single-sided and double-sided boards to multilayer constructions up to 16 layers. Its capabilities include fine-line and surface-mount technology pitches, board thicknesses from 0.008 to 0.250 inches, carbon ink contacts, oversized multilayer panels, ball grid array patterns, blind and buried vias, peelable and water-soluble masks, plated slots and edges, epoxy via plug, and controlled impedance. Materials stocked encompass FR-4, high-temperature FR-4 equivalents, Rogers, Taconic, Arlon, polyimide, Teflon, and GETEK laminates. Surface finishes offered are solder mask over bare copper, hot air solder leveling, electroless nickel/gold (including bondable gold), electroless white tin, electroless silver, screenable silver and carbon, and heavy copper layers. The 25,000-square-foot facility employs more than 40 people and has produced over 100 million rigid PCBs, with annual revenue exceeding $5 million. The company owns its equipment and recently invested over $1 million in new fabrication and testing systems.

Axon Circuit serves customers in communications, instrumentation and controls, consumer electronics, medical devices, automotive, and military sectors. Its clientele is primarily business-to-business, built largely through referrals.

The company emphasizes an attitude of continuous improvement, personalized service, and on-time delivery. It maintains a supplier performance guarantee, offers competitive domestic and offshore quotes, and operates an internal waste treatment and reverse osmosis system to reduce environmental impact.

about:
AZ Prototype, Inc. operates from a facility in Mesa, Arizona, where it was founded in 2009 as a woman‑owned private electronics contract manufacturer. The company began with a focus on providing flexible, quick‑turn manufacturing services for both prototype and production projects, aiming to deliver high‑quality, cost‑effective solutions.

The shop specializes in printed circuit board assembly, wire and cable harness assembly, and electro‑mechanical box builds. It runs MYDATA MY19 and YAMAHA YSM20 pick‑and‑place equipment, offers a 24‑ to 48‑hour quick‑turn prototype service, and maintains a flexible manufacturing schedule with no general inventory. Turnkey services cover the full product lifecycle from prototype to volume production.

AZ Prototype serves a wide range of businesses across the electronics sector, supporting customers who need prototype runs as well as ongoing production volumes. Its AS9100 certification indicates work for aerospace and defense programs, though the company does not publicly list specific industry verticals or named clients.

The company emphasizes meeting customer expectations through on‑time delivery, continuous improvement, and adherence to IPC workmanship standards for electronic assemblies, cable harnesses, and soldered connections. Its quality system is built on ISO 9001 and AS9100 requirements.

name: B & G Medical
old_description: We are a custom fastener manufacturer and precision parts supplier with artisanal expertise, meticulously crafting each product to exceed expectations. Our
about:
B&G Manufacturing operates from Hatfield, Pennsylvania, where it has been a family-owned and -managed business for over six decades. The company traces its roots to a founding commitment to manufacturing excellence, though the exact year is not publicly stated. Today, the firm remains under family leadership, emphasizing expertise, integrity, and reliability as core values.

The company produces custom fasteners and precision components through a vertically integrated operation that spans turning, Swiss-style turning, milling (including dedicated PEEK), deep-hole gun drilling, forging, bolt bending, shearing, thread rolling, thread cutting, grinding, wire and sink EDM, heat treating, titanium anodizing, laser marking, ultrasonic cleaning, shot peening, glass beading, passivation, and metallurgical evaluation. Its Hatfield facility houses more than 10,000 standard part numbers in stock for next-day shipment, while also running custom prototypes and large-scale production runs tracked via SAP ERP and MII systems.

B&G serves four primary sectors: medical (spinal implants, surgical instrumentation, bone-fracture and trauma devices), energy (nuclear, hydroelectric, natural-gas, and coal power generation), oil and gas (exploration, extraction, refining, and transport in harsh environments), and aerospace and defense (fasteners for ships, aircraft, and submarines). Customers include OEMs, military agencies, and nuclear power operators requiring compliance with ASME Section III, 10 CFR 50, and FDA 21 CFR 820.

The firm differentiates itself through full vertical integration, which shortens lead times and tightens supply-chain control; a 90-percent on-time delivery record; real-time quality tracking via SAP; and a family culture that prioritizes long-term customer relationships over transactional sales.

name: B & J Food Equipment
old_description: At B&J Food Equipment we pride ourselves on our commitment to offer our customers the highest quality products
about:
B & J Food Equipment was founded in 1994 in Kansas City, Missouri, by Bill and Nancy Mosburg as a family‑run venture to sell used equipment from their small restaurant chain. The company expanded to St. Louis in 2005, adding a distribution center that enabled national chain fulfillment. In 2017 the business was acquired by Innovative Foodservice Group, though the Mosburg family remains involved in daily operations. Today the firm operates cash‑and‑carry showrooms in both Kansas City, Kansas, and St. Louis, Missouri.

The company operates as a foodservice equipment distributor and service provider, offering new and used commercial kitchen equipment, smallwares, janitorial supplies, exhaust hoods, and front‑of‑house items such as china, glassware, and silverware. Beyond product sales, B & J provides design and appraisal services, CAD‑based kitchen layout, project staging, mechanical contracting for hood installations, full restaurant package delivery, and dedicated delivery scheduling. Its two showrooms double as distribution hubs serving independent operators and multi‑unit chains alike.

Primary customers include independent restaurants, regional chains, and national brands such as Firehouse Subs and Subway. The firm also supplies institutional and hospitality foodservice operations, leveraging buying‑group affiliations with ABC and IFED and the broader Innovative Foodservice Group network that extends distribution across the Southeast.

The founders started the business to liquidate surplus restaurant equipment, and the company emphasizes practical, veteran‑driven advice over catalog‑only selling, promising a single‑source solution and white‑glove service from design through installation.

The business supplies automotive paint, body shop equipment, and related materials to independent auto body shops and repair facilities throughout the greater Philadelphia region. name: BCI - Buckeye Corrugated Sioux Falls
old_description: Founded in 2009, Altar’d State set out to create a unique retail experience with a greater purpose. Known for stylish…
about:
BCI's Sioux Falls division operates from a facility at 4501 North 2nd Avenue in Sioux Falls, South Dakota. The division traces its roots to 1975 when it was established as a leader in custom corrugated packaging across the upper Midwest and Central Plains. Buckeye Corrugated (BCI) acquired the operation in 2013, and it is now led by General Manager Chad Sabers alongside a management team that includes Area Vice President Adam Williams, Region Sales Manager Nic Poshusta, Controller Mary Jo Galles, and Creative and Client Services Manager Vladimir Sobolev.

The division manufactures a broad range of corrugated packaging solutions, from standard boxes to complex multi-printed packages featuring unique cuts, folds, and joints. Capabilities include multi-color printing, die cutting, scoring, and structural design for point-of-purchase displays. The team emphasizes rapid turnaround, describing its timeframe as unparalleled, though specific lead times or production volumes are not published.

Customers span food and beverage, automotive aftermarket, and consumer packaged goods. Public case studies reference work for Gallo Family Vineyards on a Meals on Wheels display, Alpura for dairy product launches, and Royal Purple for off-shelf retail programs. The division also supports retail execution with end-cap and POP display assembly services.

The company's stated differentiators center on a culture of continuous improvement—captured in the mantra "outwork yesterday"—and a commitment to domestic production summed up by the tagline "Built for Performance. Made in America. Delivered Coast-to-Coast." The focus is on making the customer experience transformational rather than merely transactional.

about:
BG Nebraska operates from Lincoln, Nebraska, serving as a regional distributor of BG automotive maintenance products across a broad swath of Nebraska and Iowa. The company does not disclose its founding year or ownership structure, and no founders are named in its public materials.

The business supplies BG's line of professional-grade automotive chemicals and equipment, and couples that supply with on-site training and consultation for technicians and service advisors. Its supported systems cover fuel, engine, transmission, brakes, power steering, cooling, battery, drive line, and climate control. A seven-person sales team — including Jason Allen, Heath Aufenkamp, Mark Andersen, Mike Morgan, Justin Galaska, Danny Taylor, and Kyle Smithhisler — works directly with shops, though total headcount and facility size are not published.

Customers are independent repair facilities and dealerships in counties such as Douglas, Lancaster, Sarpy, and Pottawattamie. Testimonials cite shops in Council Bluffs, Iowa, and Omaha, Nebraska, where representatives have assisted with technical diagnosis, sales processes, and warranty claims on transmission and other major repairs.

BG Nebraska emphasizes that its products are proven in the field and that its representatives provide both technical and sales coaching, aiming to increase shop profitability and customer retention through proper system maintenance.
